<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide for drawing a precise system design diagram of TemplateKit, tailored to its role as an open-source template rendering library in Swift. Follow these instructions to capture its architecture, component relationships, and extensibility points.

1. Identify project type and purpose  
   • Project type: Open-source Swift library (Vapor ecosystem).  
   • Purpose: Parse template files, build an AST, and render text output by merging templates with user‐provided data.  

2. Main architectural components  
   Group your diagram into the following high-level modules (use boxes or swimlanes):  
   A. Template Source Input  
   B. Parser & AST  
   C. Data Model & Encoder  
   D. Rendering Pipeline  
   E. Tag Extensions  
   F. Caching & Utilities  
   G. Integration Point (ViewRenderer / Vapor)  

3. Component breakdown and interactions  
   1. Template Source Input  
      - Template files (e.g. “index.leaf”), raw text.  
      - Arrow → feeds into the Parser & AST.  
   2. Parser & AST (Sources/TemplateKit/AST & Pipeline/TemplateParser)  
      - TemplateByteScanner: tokenizes input.  
      - TemplateParser: produces AST nodes (TemplateSyntax, TemplateTag, TemplateExpression, etc.).  
      - AST data structures (TemplateConditional, TemplateIterator, TemplateRaw, etc.)  
      - Arrow → hands AST to the Rendering Pipeline.  
   3. Data Model & Encoder (Sources/TemplateKit/Data)  
      - TemplateData: unified data type.  
      - TemplateDataEncoder: encodes Swift types (structs, primitives) into TemplateData.  
      - Arrow (bidirectional) ↔ Rendering Pipeline: renderer pulls values by key from TemplateData.  
   4. Rendering Pipeline (Sources/TemplateKit/Pipeline & ViewRenderer)  
      - TemplateRenderer: walks the AST, invokes TagRenderer for each tag node.  
      - PlaintextRenderer: handles nodes that are raw text or unparsed segments.  
      - TemplateSerializer: serializes AST for caching or reuse.  
      - Arrow → produces final String output.  
   5. Tag Extensions (Sources/TemplateKit/Tag)  
      - TagRenderer & TagContext: generic plugin interfaces.  
      - Built-in tags: Var, If (conditional), Loop (iterator), DateFormat, Uppercase/Lowercase, Contains, Count, Print, Raw, Comment, Capitalize.  
      - Show each tag as a sub-box under “Tag Extensions,” with arrows from Rendering Pipeline to each Tag implementation.  
   6. Caching & Utilities (Sources/TemplateKit/Pipeline/ASTCache & Utilities)  
      - ASTCache: caches parsed AST keyed by template path.  
      - Utilities: HTMLEscape, TemplateError, Exports.  
      - Arrow from Parser & AST → ASTCache (store) and ASTCache → Rendering Pipeline (retrieve).  
   7. Integration Point  
      - ViewRenderer & View: conform to Vapor’s View protocol.  
      - Arrow from Rendering Pipeline output → Vapor HTTP Response in a web app context.  

4. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   • Separation of Concerns: parsing, data encoding, rendering, tagging, and caching are distinct modules.  
   • Plug-in architecture: tag implementations conform to a shared TagRenderer interface.  
   • Immutable AST: parsing and rendering phases are decoupled to allow caching and reuse.  
   • Swift Package Manager: Package.swift defines dependencies (no external services).  

5. Diagram tailoring guidelines for an open-source library  
   • Emphasize core pipeline (parse → AST → render).  
   • Highlight extensibility: show TagRenderer interface and built-in tags as extensions.  
   • Show integration boundary: how ViewRenderer plugs into a web framework.  

6. Visual notation recommendations  
   • Boxes or swimlanes for each module group.  
   • Arrows with labels indicating “parse,” “encode,” “render,” “cache,” “output.”  
   • Color coding:  
     – Blue for core engine (Parser, AST, Renderer)  
     – Green for Data modules  
     – Yellow for Tag extensions  
     – Orange for caching & utilities  
     – Purple for integration layer  
   • Shapes:  
     – Rounded rectangles for modules  
     – Cylinders for cache/storage (ASTCache)  
     – Document icon for template files  
   • Legend explaining colors/shapes.  

7. Essential diagram elements  
   – Clear labels on every component box.  
   – Directional arrows showing data flow and dependencies.  
   – Grouping boundaries or swimlanes to show module separation.  
   – Annotation of key technologies (Swift 4.1, SPM, Vapor integration).  

By following these steps, you will produce a system design diagram that clearly shows how TemplateKit ingests template text, builds and caches an AST, encodes user data, applies tags, renders output, and integrates with the Vapor web framework—all while exposing extensibility points for custom tags.
